{"id": "eae4c102-2768-4f46-9831-0897b4cf6777", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Both are Elastic Load Balancing types. They work at different layers of the network stack.

| | **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** | **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TLS, TCP_UDP |
| **Routing** | Content-aware. It routes on path, host header, HTTP headers, query strings, methods and source IP. | Connection-based. It routes on IP, port and protocol. |
| **Performance** | Good, with some per-request processing overhead | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency. It handles millions of requests per second and sudden traffic spikes. |
| **IP addresses** | Dynamic IPs, so you use the DNS name | One static IP per Availability Zone, with optional Elastic IPs |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions and containers | Instances, IPs and ALBs |
| **Client IP preservation** | The client IP arrives in the `X-Forwarded-For` header. | Preserved natively for instance targets. Proxy Protocol v2 is also supported. |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023), but optional |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS and supports SNI | Terminates or passes through TLS |
| **Built-in features** | Authentication through Cognito or OIDC, redirects, fixed responses, WAF integration | PrivateLink (endpoint services) and long-lived connections |

**When to choose an ALB**
- You run HTTP/HTTPS web apps, microservices or APIs.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, for example `/api` and `/images` going to different target groups.
- You want to route to Lambda functions.
- You need WAF protection or built-in user authentication.

**When to choose an NLB**
- You need extreme performance or very low latency.
- Your clients need static IPs, for example for firewall allow-listing.
- You handle non-HTTP protocols such as gaming, IoT, VoIP, DNS or custom TCP/UDP.
- You want to expose a service through AWS PrivateLink.

**Using them together:** You can put an NLB in front of an ALB. This gives you static IPs and PrivateLink support while keeping Layer 7 routing.

I can also compare the two against your own setup. For example, I could look at which load balancers you currently run in your account.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
